story: What a good debugger can do
text: > I should mention that the perfect debugger doesn’t exist It may not exist, but this demo has got to be the closest thing to the perfect debugger I've ever seen: [VIDEO]

Allan Blomquist's tooling demo they mention is incredible, go watch it: [VIDEO] Really sells the value of having a tight developer feedback loop: it shows hot reloading for code and graphics, a reversible debugger, live profiling with flame graphs, a data inspector with data breakpoints, time travel inspection with a scrub bar, session sharing and replay with the same scrub bar and direct links from the call stack to a breakpoint, and more. Above the many niggles they had with Rust itself, this greatly helps me understand why Rust left them wanting more from their working environment. They say they've switched back to Unity with [LINK] to try to capture some of that, and now I see why. (It's a shame that hot reloading tooling in Rust wasn't ready for them yet, but I see why they've moved on instead of waiting/contributing.)

story: GTFL – A Graphical Terminal for Common Lisp
text: Yes, I'm a big fan of Bret Victor's work. I share his Inventing on Principle talk on a near yearly basis. I've seen light table years ago and thought it looked really neat, but I haven't looked into it much as it wasn't directly applicable to my environments. But, probably worth a look for ideas. On the topic of time-travel debugging, have you seen the demo: [VIDEO] (Tomorrow Corporation Tech Demo) Very impressive, worth a watch.

He mentions Common Lisp as something he did a game in, and you can see the link he praises [VIDEO] as basically a very well-developed Lisp image approach with timetravel debugging etc aimed at game dev. So the implicit comparison to Lisps is sort of a big undercurrent to this whole article.

story: Show HN: C# Game Engine with its own scripting language and IDE
text: Reminds me of the Tomorrow Corporation (developer of World of Goo) tech demo: [VIDEO] Their entire stack is custom (language, compiler, IDE, build system, engine). Has neat features like time-travelling debugging and instant hot-reloading for code and assets.
